entities.name: PMID:27510437
observations: In 60 male Sprague-Dawley rats with experimental periodontitis, melatonin added to irradiation significantly lowered oxidative stress index, 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine, malondialdehyde, and C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen versus irradiated periodontitis controls.

Melatonin significantly reduced alveolar bone destruction and periodontal attachment-level damage versus irradiated periodontitis controls; radiation and melatonin dose/timing were unavailable from the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: PMID:39614289
observations: In 40 female Sprague-Dawley rats with ligature-induced periodontitis, a single 5-Gy radiotherapy dose was followed by melatonin 10 mg/kg for 15 days.

Compared with irradiated periodontitis controls, melatonin significantly improved TOS/TAS, inflammatory, apoptotic, and bone-remodeling outcomes and limited buccal, lingual, and furcal alveolar bone loss; destruction was close to control levels.
Melatonin was not significantly different from amifostine across measured parameters.

entities.name: Melatonin
observations: In two directly relevant irradiated-rat experimental-periodontitis studies, melatonin improved radiation-associated oxidative-stress measures and reduced periodontal or alveolar bone breakdown versus irradiated periodontitis controls.

entities.name: Experimental periodontitis
observations: The directly relevant evidence used rat models of experimental or ligature-induced periodontitis combined with irradiation.

entities.name: Melatonin protection
observations: Across two direct rat studies, melatonin reduced radiation-associated oxidative stress and periodontal/alveolar bone destruction compared with irradiated periodontitis controls.
Evidence is preclinical and limited to two direct animal studies.
